blocks.text: Hello Robert,
Thank you for the investor list. It covers the mix we asked for, long-standing holders as well as more recent ones, and we will not contact anyone on it until you have approved the introduction note.

You asked how we will introduce ourselves. The note goes out under your name. It says that {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} has asked an outside firm to gather candid views on how the company is seen, and it asks each person for a short call. It also says that nothing they tell us will be attributed to them by name. I have a draft, and Julie is reading it now.

The coverage review is on track. Kimberly has finished collecting the online and social coverage for the period we agreed, and I am working through print and trade. Nothing in it so far changes the plan.
You will have the draft note from me early next week for your edits.
Thanks
Robert,

We agree with you about the word "audit." To an investor it can suggest that something has gone wrong, and that is not the impression we want the note to leave. We will describe the conversations instead as part of a periodic review of how {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} communicates with the people who follow it, which is accurate and, in our experience, far less likely to prompt an anxious call.

We would also suggest one addition, if you are comfortable with it. A sentence stating that we will not discuss results, outlook, or anything the company has not already made public tends to put investors at ease, and it gives you some protection as well.
Michelle will send you the draft with both changes marked, so that you can approve it in a single pass.
Thanks
Hello Robert,

Thank you for turning the note around so quickly. Your edit to the closing paragraph is in, and the note is now final. It can go out from your address whenever suits you, and I will follow up with each person to book a time once it has.

On sitting in on the calls, we recommend against it. Investors speak more freely to an outside firm when no one from {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} is on the line. You will still see every theme that comes out of the conversations, without names attached.
The next step is yours. Please send the note and copy me on it, so I know when to start booking.
Thanks
Robert,

I will take the investor conversations myself, with Kimberly on each call to keep notes. Michelle will look after the scheduling, and she will also speak informally with the reporters who cover the company, most of whom she already knows.

We would very much like to speak with your leadership team as well, and ideally before the first investor calls take place. Hearing first how {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} sees itself gives us something against which to measure the outside views, and it tends to make the investor conversations sharper.
Could you let us know, by the end of this week, which colleagues you would like us to include? Michelle will then arrange a time directly with each of them.
Thanks
Working Session Notes: Reputation Audit for {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}}
Held by video call. These notes record the principal points of discussion and the actions agreed, and are circulated to those who attended.
Attending

items: Julie Hill, Managing Partner, Ashcombe Advisory Partners
Michelle Rose, Communications Associate, Ashcombe Advisory Partners
Kimberly Le, Communications Analyst, Ashcombe Advisory Partners

blocks.text: Why we met

We met to take stock of the audit so far and to agree how the stakeholder conversations should proceed from here. The observations recorded below are provisional. They rest on the coverage review and on a small number of interviews, and we would expect some of them to be refined as the remaining conversations are held.
What the coverage shows so far

Kimberly Le presented the review of online and social coverage, and Michelle Rose the review of print and trade coverage. Taken together, coverage of {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} over the period reviewed has been largely neutral in tone. It has concentrated on financial announcements, with comparatively little attention paid to the business itself or to the people who lead it.

Kimberly Le also noted that a small number of older articles continue to appear prominently in search results and are occasionally cited in newer pieces. Robert Smith asked whether this was unusual. We explained that it is common among companies of a similar size, and that it bears more on how a new investor first encounters the company than on how it is regarded by those who already follow it.
Stakeholder conversations

The leadership interviews were held first, as agreed, and are nearly complete. The introduction note has gone to every investor on the agreed list and most have replied. Julie Hill has since held the first of the investor conversations, with Kimberly Le keeping notes, and Michelle Rose has begun informal conversations with reporters who cover the company.

The early investor conversations suggest that management is regarded as credible and the financial reporting as clear. Where investors hesitated was in describing the company's longer-term direction in their own words. We were careful to say that this rests on very few conversations and may not hold across the full set.

Robert Smith asked that the remaining conversations include a question on how investors would prefer to hear from the company between formal announcements. We agreed that this would be a useful addition, and it will be put to every investor from this point on.
How the findings will be shared

We discussed how the findings should be presented once the conversations are complete. Robert Smith asked that they come to him first and then to the leadership team, and we agreed that the readout will take place in those two stages. We also confirmed that no comment will be attributed to an individual investor or reporter by name.
Agreed actions

rows: Add the question on communication between formal announcements to the investor interview guide
Prepare a short note on the older articles that rank highly in search results, with options for addressing them
Continue informal conversations with reporters who cover the company
Confirm who from the leadership team will attend the second stage of the readout

blocks.text: Our next step is to complete the investor conversations, after which we will meet again to review them together. Michelle Rose will propose times for that session to Robert Smith in the course of next week.
Status Report: Reputation Audit for {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}}
Prepared by Michelle Rose, Communications Associate, with Kimberly Le and Julie Hill of Ashcombe Advisory Partners.
Where the audit stands

The audit has reached its midpoint on schedule and within scope. The coverage review is complete, and so are the leadership interviews. More than half of the investor conversations have been held, and the conversations with reporters are under way. We have started to bring the material together, and nothing we have heard so far calls for a change to the plan.
Since the working session

Kimberly Le finished the review of online and social coverage, and I finished print and trade. The picture we described at the working session has held. Coverage of {{fact:f:E-2024-001.client}} is mostly neutral in tone and concentrates on financial announcements. There is little about the business itself, its customers, or the people who run it. Where the company does appear in a broader industry story, it is usually named in passing.

Kimberly Le also sent you her note on the older articles that still rank highly in search results. It sets out the options, from leaving them alone to publishing newer material that will over time push them down. We will hold any recommendation on this until the findings are complete, because the right answer depends on what investors tell us about how they first came across the company.

Julie Hill completed the leadership interviews. The leadership team gives a consistent account of where the company is going and why, from one person to the next. That is useful to us. It suggests that whatever gap the audit finds will lie in how the strategy is explained to people outside the company.

Julie Hill has also held most of the investor conversations, with Kimberly Le on each call to take notes. The question you asked us to add, on how investors would like to hear from the company between formal announcements, has been put in every conversation since the working session. The early pattern has held. Investors regard management as credible and find the financial reporting clear. Most of them find it harder to describe the company's longer-term direction, and a number said they hear from the company only around its formal announcements.

I have spoken informally with several of the reporters who cover the company. They describe it as responsive when they call. They also say they rarely hear from it unprompted, and none could recall the company bringing them a story. That matches what investors are telling us, and we will treat the two as parts of the same finding.
The coming weeks

The remaining investor conversations are booked over the next two weeks, and I expect to finish the reporter conversations in the same period. Once both are done, Kimberly Le and I will draft a single findings document that draws together the coverage review, the leadership interviews, and the investor and reporter conversations. Julie Hill will review the draft before it comes to you.

As agreed at the working session, the findings will come to you first and then go to the leadership team. Recommendations will follow the findings and will be built from them. We will not put recommendations in front of the leadership team until the findings have been discussed.
Budget

Work to date is in line with the engagement budget of {{fact:f:E-2024-001.fee}}, and the effort spent so far matches the plan. We do not expect to ask for any change to the budget or the scope. If the leadership readout leads to a request for further work, we will scope it separately and agree it with you before any of it starts.
Points we are watching

The investor sample is small by design. Its views are a strong indication, not a measurement, and we will say so plainly in the findings. We will also show which views were widely shared and which came from one or two people.

A few investors on the list have not yet confirmed a time. If they have not done so by the time the other conversations are finished, we will close the interview period on schedule and record in the findings who was not reached.

The finding on longer-term direction touches on how the leadership team describes its own strategy, and it needs careful handling. We will present it with the evidence behind it, in the investors' own words where we can, and it will reach you before anyone else sees it.
The next step is the last of the investor conversations. I will write to you once it has been held, with proposed times for the first readout.
